clue.text: English home in Spain's fantastic

definitions.meaning: the proverb says an Englishman's home is his fortress-like seat
a '... in Spain' is a daydream, an impossible fantasy

explanation.surface: A remark that the English house is fantastic when it is in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'castle in Spain' (French château en Espagne) means a pipe dream; the clue reads 'castle in Spain' as fantastic, while 'English home' recalls the saying 'An Englishman's home is his castle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two idioms: the English proverb about a home being a fortress, and the old phrase for a daydream, a fortress in Spain.

clue.text: Jazzman swallowing salty concoction as a stimulant

indicators.note: the jazzman takes the mixed letters inside himself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cat is slang for a jazz musician

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of salty are mixed up

explanation.surface: A jazz musician downing a salty cocktail to perk himself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts TALYS, the rearrangement of SALTY signalled by 'concoction', between the C and A-T of CAT, giving CA-TALYS-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is something that speeds up or provokes change, a stimulant in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Having been turned out, squats in the same old place

indicators.note: the words having been turned over are reshuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Squatters evicted from a building simply settle back where they were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having been turned' signals an anagram of OUT SQUATS; the surface makes 'turned out' sound like an eviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Status quo is Latin for the existing state of affairs, things left where they always were.

clue.text: Dead on time? No

definitions.meaning: the ... so-and-so is someone who has died
not punctual, arriving after the expected hour

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deceased (the late king) and tardy, the opposite of punctual.

clue.text: Student mixed spice with lots of dill

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters are blended into a new arrangement
lots of the word dill, but not all of it: its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A cookery pupil blending spices with plenty of dill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of' trims DILL to DIL; 'mixed' then rearranges SPICE plus DIL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower or pupil who learns from a master.

clue.text: Shut up! The Demon King is appearing!

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
R stands for rex, Latin for king
on means appearing, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A pantomime announcement that the Demon King has come on stage, with the audience told to hush.
explanation.walkthrough: The Demon King is the villain of a British pantomime; here the words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone up in the sense of locking them away is to jail them.

clue.text: Partners drum up custom on Rhode Island

indicators.note: to drum up is to stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Business partners trying to drum up trade on Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drum up' rearranges CUSTOM, ON and RI together.
explanation.definitionFit: A consortium is an association of companies acting together, a group of partners.

clue.text: Request model to display fashion feature

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A request for a model to show off a fashion detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a catwalk model but is the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn into fabric, a design detail of clothing.

clue.text: Among the cognoscenti, Rembrandt is regarded as perfect

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the run of words the cognoscenti, Rembrandt

explanation.surface: Art connoisseurs consider Rembrandt flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole and unbroken, complete in every part.

clue.text: Northern cry of welcome

definitions.meaning: in Scotland and northern England to ... is to weep
to welcome someone is to receive them warmly

explanation.definitionFit: The Scots verb means to weep, while the standard verb means to receive with a salutation.

clue.text: Characteristic alternative from one who's seen both sides

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Choosing between a feature and an option, from someone who has seen both points of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who's seen both sides' suggests a fair-minded person, but here it is someone who has served both sides: a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat betrays his own side to the enemy, so he has belonged to both camps.

clue.text: Joke man finds a bit rich

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A man thinks a joke is a little too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit rich' suggests an unfair remark, but is the definition: strongly flavoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means sharply strong in taste or smell, as a rich sauce can be.

clue.text: Praise for 200% return

indicators.note: return means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: two hundred percent is double, or dual

explanation.surface: Praise given for a two-hundred-percent return on an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to extol or commend.

clue.text: Priest- Christian of sorts -cuts woman with chopper

indicators.note: the priest and the Christian cut into the woman, sitting inside her

parts.note: her is a woman, as a pronoun
Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel
a Copt is an Egyptian Christian

explanation.surface: A violent tale of a priest, some kind of Christian, attacking a woman with an axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' reads as an axe but is slang for a rotorcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopper is the informal name for a rotary-winged aircraft.

clue.text: Banter in its own right maintaining one standard

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the phrase keeps other pieces inside it

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, in its own right
I is the Roman numeral one
a standard is a flag

explanation.surface: Banter in its own right that keeps to one standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, mocking talk, teasing chatter.

clue.text: Engineers replace gunners in Welch's follow-up

indicators.note: replace means one piece is swapped out for another in the name

parts.note: Raquel Welch is the film actress, so her first name is the piece
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
SE is an abbreviation for the Society of Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers stand in for gunners in Welch's next film.
explanation.walkthrough: Welch is Raquel Welch, the actress; swapping RA for SE in her first name gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is a work that continues the story of an earlier one.

clue.text: Carriers charge for putting tip of spoon into soup

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside
into shows where the first letter goes: within the soup

parts.note: potage is a thick soup

indicators.note: the tip of the word spoon is its first letter

explanation.surface: Being charged for dipping a spoon tip into one's soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... into' puts S (tip of spoon) inside POTAGE, a French thick soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee the mail carriers charge for delivery.

clue.text: Grinder was late for the barbecue, so Spooner says

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: to be late for something is to have missed it
a grill is a barbecue

explanation.surface: Someone missed the barbecue, according to Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MISSED GRILL' with its opening sounds swapped gives 'grist mill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gristmill is a mill for grinding grain.

clue.text: Lean to leader's philosophy

parts.note: lean means thin
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: A leaning towards the leader's philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean to' suggests a leaning; here 'to' just links THIN and KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking can mean a body of ideas or way of thought, as in current political thinking.

clue.text: Military HQ's flag carrying label

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the flag holds the label within it

parts.note: a penon is an old spelling of pennon, a long narrow flag
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Military headquarters' flag bearing a label.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided building in Virginia houses the US Department of Defense.

clue.text: Politically correct horse swapped for car

indicators.note: the letters are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: A politically correct choice: trading in a horse for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Porsche is a German maker of sports cars.

clue.text: Girl keeping leg outstretched

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A girl keeps her leg stretched out.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on the back, stretched out.

clue.text: Passion confers a right to be grim

parts.note: dour means grim, stern

explanation.surface: Passion grants someone the right to be gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or fervour.

clue.text: Stout insect gutted fly

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the first and last letters of fly

explanation.surface: A stout insect gutting a fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means burly and heavily built.

clue.text: Where to look for love-token? Third on the left

definitions.meaning: an engagement or wedding band is worn on this digit
it is the third finger of the left hand, counting from the index finger

explanation.definitionFit: The digit that wears a wedding band is the third finger of the left hand.

clue.text: Rumour of bouquet received

annotationWithheld.why: Rumour of bouquet received (5): NOSE gives the bouquet, but no word supplies the I or signals a homophone that gives NOISE; probably cut or misread, no scan to check

clue.text: Reinstate something the editor trashed initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of each of these four words

explanation.surface: An editor restores something they had binned.
explanation.walkthrough: The proofreader's mark, Latin for 'let it stand', is spelt by the first letters of the last four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is an editor's instruction to restore a deleted passage.

clue.text: Run into the red?

definitions.meaning: to run at a gentle pace
a Trotskyist is into red, left-wing politics

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a jog and is also short for a Trotskyist, a left-winger.

clue.text: Ring road round capital generates paperwork

indicators.note: round means placed around the capital, so it sits between the other pieces

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A ring road around the capital creates paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: MI is the M1, the London-to-Yorkshire motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper, so it is literally work with paper.

clue.text: Agriculture in distant China

parts.note: far means distant
Ming is a famous Chinese dynasty, and its porcelain is china

explanation.surface: Agriculture in faraway China.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming is the working of land and livestock for food.

clue.text: Say king and Arab ruler return to surface again

indicators.note: return means all the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) means say
R is for rex, Latin for king
emeer is a variant spelling of emir, an Arab ruler

explanation.surface: A king and an Arab ruler, say, come back to reappear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the whole run EG R EMEER, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-emerge is to come up into view again.

clue.text: Hot as illicit kisses?

explanation.definitionFit: Taken unlawfully, as hot goods are; and the phrase for secret kisses snatched on the sly.
